breakfast.name: Bouillie de Mil
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh milk or powdered milk
instructions: Mix millet flour with 1 cup of cold water to form a smooth paste.
Bring remaining 3 cups of water to a boil in a pot.
Slowly pour the millet paste into the boiling water, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until thick and smooth.
Stir in sugar, milk, and vanilla. Serve warm in bowls.
breakfast.description: A smooth, warm millet porridge sweetened with sugar and enriched with milk, the standard breakfast across Burkina Faso's households.

breakfast.name: Beignets Burkinabe
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, nutmeg, and salt in a bowl.
Add eggs and warm water, stirring until a thick, sticky dough forms.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 170C (340F).
Drop spoonfuls of dough into the hot oil and fry until golden brown and puffed, about 3 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm, optionally dusted with extra sugar.
breakfast.description: Golden fried dough balls with a hint of nutmeg, sold at every market and street corner in Ouagadougou as a beloved morning snack.

breakfast.name: Kooko (Millet Porridge)
instructions: Mix millet flour with cold water to smooth paste
Bring more water to boil
Stir in millet paste gradually
Cook until thick, stirring constantly
Thin to drinkable consistency
Add tamarind juice, sugar, lemon
Serve warm or cool
breakfast.description: Tangy millet porridge — Burkina's everyday breakfast drink, thinned enough to sip from a bowl. The tamarind gives it a distinctive sourness.

lunch.name: Riz Gras
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and brown the beef cubes on all sides.
Add onion and garlic, cooking until softened.
Stir in blended tomatoes, tomato paste, and Maggi cube. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add carrots, green beans, and water. Bring to a boil.
Add rice, stir, cover tightly, and reduce heat to low.
Cook for 25 minutes until rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid. Fluff and serve.
lunch.description: Burkina Faso's festive one-pot rice cooked in a rich tomato and meat sauce with vegetables, a celebration dish enjoyed across the country.

lunch.name: To with Sauce Gombo
ingredients: 2 cups millet flour or corn flour
instructions: Bring 3 cups of water to a boil. Gradually add millet flour, stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon until it forms a thick, firm dough. Set aside.
Heat palm oil and saute onion until translucent.
Add tomatoes and soumbala, cooking for 5 minutes.
Add chopped okra and smoked fish. Add 1 cup of water and simmer for 15 minutes until okra is slimy and tender.
Season with salt. Serve the to in mounds with the okra sauce ladled over the top.
lunch.description: The daily staple of Burkina Faso: firm millet dough served with a thick, slimy okra sauce enriched with smoked fish and soumbala.

lunch.name: Riz Gras (Fat Rice)
instructions: Brown meat, set aside
Sauté onion, garlic, add tomato paste and tomatoes
Add water, return meat, simmer 15 min
Add rice and vegetables
Cook until rice absorbs liquid and is tender
The tomato and meat juices flavor every grain
lunch.description: One-pot tomato rice cooked in meat broth — the popular Burkinabè lunch. Simple, deeply flavorful, always feeds a crowd.

dinner.name: Poulet Bicyclette
ingredients: 1 whole free-range chicken, cut into pieces
Sliced tomatoes and onions for garnish
instructions: Marinate chicken pieces in mustard, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, paprika, salt, and pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a large skillet and sear chicken pieces on all sides until golden.
Add sliced onion rings, cover, and cook on medium-low heat for 35 minutes, turning occasionally.
Uncover and increase heat to crisp the skin for the last 5 minutes.
Serve with sliced tomatoes, raw onion rings, and fried plantains.
dinner.description: The famous grilled free-range chicken of Burkina Faso, named after the bicycles used to transport them, served with onions and fried plantains.

dinner.name: Ragout d'Igname
instructions: Heat palm oil and brown the meat on all sides.
Add onion and garlic, cooking until fragrant.
Stir in blended tomatoes, tomato paste, and Maggi cube. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add yam cubes and enough water to just cover. Add the whole habanero.
Simmer for 20 minutes until yam is tender and sauce is thick.
Remove habanero before serving. Serve hot.
dinner.description: A hearty yam and meat stew in a rich tomato and palm oil sauce, a filling evening meal enjoyed throughout Burkina Faso.

dinner.name: Sauce Baobab (Baobab Leaf Soup)
instructions: Sauté onion in palm oil
Add tomato, cook until broken down
Add meat or fish with water
Stir in powdered baobab leaves — they thicken the sauce
Add dawadawa for deep umami
Simmer 25 min until thick and slimy-smooth
Serve over tô
dinner.description: Soup made from dried baobab leaves — a staple sauce in Burkina, thickened naturally by the leaves. Served over tô (millet paste).

snacks.name: Galettes de Niebe
ingredients: 2 cups black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and peeled
instructions: Blend soaked and peeled black-eyed peas with onion, habanero, and salt into a thick paste.
Beat the paste vigorously with a spoon until light and airy.
Heat oil in a deep pan. Drop spoonfuls of the paste into hot oil.
Fry until golden brown and crispy, about 4 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with spicy tomato sauce.
snacks.description: Crispy fried black-eyed pea fritters, a protein-rich street snack found at markets across Burkina Faso.

snacks.name: Brochettes (Grilled Meat Skewers)
ingredients: Suya spice: ground peanuts, chili, ginger, garlic, paprika
instructions: Thread meat and onion onto skewers
Brush with oil, season with suya spice and salt
Grill over charcoal, turning frequently
Serve immediately with more suya spice for dipping
snacks.description: Charcoal-grilled meat skewers dusted with suya spice — sold at every roadside grill stand in Ouagadougou.

snacks.name: Brochettes de Bœuf (Street Grilled Beef Skewers)
ingredients: Suya spice: ground peanuts, cayenne, ginger, onion powder, paprika, salt
instructions: Cut beef into 2cm cubes
Make suya spice mix: toast and grind peanuts, mix with cayenne, ginger, onion powder, paprika, salt
Coat beef cubes generously in spice mix
Thread onto skewers
Grill over charcoal, turning frequently, until charred outside but juicy inside — 8-10 min
Serve with raw sliced onion and mustard on the side
In Ouagadougou, these are everywhere after dark — the charcoal smoke and spice aroma fill entire neighborhoods
snacks.description: Street-grilled beef skewers coated in a peanut-spice crust — Ouagadougou's night food. The Sahel version of suya, served with raw onion and mustard. West African street food videos featuring these smoky skewers consistently go viral for the charcoal grilling atmosphere.

desserts.name: Gonre
instructions: Peel bananas and mash them roughly in a bowl.
Mix in peanut flour, honey, cinnamon, and salt.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the mixture into the skillet and flatten slightly.
Cook until golden brown on each side, about 3 minutes per side.
Serve warm as a sweet treat.
desserts.description: Sweet banana and peanut cakes lightly pan-fried, a simple and nourishing dessert made from two of Burkina Faso's abundant crops.

desserts.name: Dèguè (Millet and Yogurt)
instructions: Steam millet couscous until tender
Cool completely
Mix with yogurt and sugar
Add vanilla or nutmeg
Serve cold
desserts.description: Chilled yogurt with tiny millet pearls — sweet, creamy, refreshing. Shared across West Africa but beloved in Burkina.

drinks.name: Bissap
instructions: Bring water to a boil and add dried hibiscus flowers. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Strain the liquid into a pitcher, pressing the flowers to extract all flavor.
Stir in sugar while still warm until dissolved. Add vanilla and lime juice.
Refrigerate until cold. Serve over ice with fresh mint leaves.
drinks.description: A vibrant ruby-red hibiscus tea sweetened with sugar and brightened with lime, the most popular refreshing drink in Burkina Faso.

drinks.name: Dolo
instructions: Soak sorghum grain in water for 24 hours, then drain and spread on a damp cloth.
Keep the grain moist and covered for 3 days until it sprouts.
Sun-dry the sprouted grain, then grind it coarsely.
Mix the ground malt with water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 3 hours, adding water as needed.
Strain the liquid and let it cool. Allow to ferment naturally for 1-2 days.
Serve at room temperature in calabash cups.
drinks.description: Traditional sorghum beer brewed by women in Burkina Faso, a mildly alcoholic, tangy drink central to social and ceremonial life.

drinks.name: Zoom Koom (Millet Flour Drink)
instructions: Mix millet flour with cold water until smooth
Strain through cloth
Add ginger juice, sugar, lemon
Add pineapple juice if desired
Serve very cold
drinks.description: Gingery millet drink — Burkina's refreshment of choice on hot days. Sold in plastic bags by street vendors.
